What makes foxes so amazing?

A clever hunter, the fox is a relative of the dog. Its hearing is so sharp it can even pick up the sound of prey hidden under the snow.

We've gathered all sorts of stories about foxes here — fox facts, fox hunting, fox ecology, and more.

content.text:
Nature and science facts about foxes

With its excellent hearing and sense of smell, a fox can detect even the faint sound of small prey hidden in the grass or under the snow. When it finds prey, it does a unique hunt — leaping high into the air and driving down with its front paws (the mousing pounce). Its long, bushy tail keeps it balanced while running and covers its nose and paws to keep out the cold while sleeping. As an omnivore that eats both meat and berries, it can live in all kinds of environments.

Great points to observe together

Point out things like the big ears (hearing), the pouncing hunt, the tail (balance and blanket), and being omnivorous (adaptable). It's fun to talk together about "Why does a fox leap up high to hunt?"

Parent guide — how to spark curiosity

Show a video of a fox "hearing sounds under the snow and leaping up to hunt." Compare the traits it shares with dogs and puppies (ears, nose, tail), and connecting it to the "crafty fox" of old folktales makes it even more engaging.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. How does a fox hunt?
A. With its keen hearing it listens for hidden prey, then leaps high into the air and drives down with its front paws in a pouncing hunt.

Q. What do foxes eat?
A. They are omnivores that eat both meat and berries. That's why they can live in all kinds of environments.

Q. How can we observe them at home?
A. Watching a video of the pouncing hunt, comparing its traits with a dog's, and connecting it to the "crafty fox" folktales all work well.
